terms.sub: Osteology of the Skull and Foramina
clues: An H-shaped sutural junction on the lateral aspect of the neurocranium.
It marks the meeting point of the frontal, parietal, squamous temporal, and sphenoid bones.
Fractures at this thin area frequently lacerate the underlying anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery.

terms.sub: Osteology of the Skull and Foramina
clues: An oval opening located in the posterior part of the greater wing of the sphenoid bone.
It connects the middle cranial fossa with the infratemporal fossa.
It transmits the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve and the accessory meningeal artery.
A flat quadrilateral muscle forming the muscular substance of the cheek.
It is innervated by the facial nerve and helps hold food between the occlusal surfaces of the molars.
The parotid duct pierces this muscle opposite the upper second molar tooth.
A sensory branch arising by two roots that encircle the middle meningeal artery in the infratemporal fossa.
It ascends posterior to the temporomandibular joint to supply skin of the temple and auricle.
It carries postganglionic parasympathetic secretomotor fibers from the otic ganglion to the parotid gland.

terms.sub: Temporal, Infratemporal Fossae and Muscles of Mastication
clues: A short, thick two-headed muscle situated in the infratemporal fossa.
It inserts into the pterygoid fovea of the mandible and the articular disc of the temporomandibular joint.
It is the only muscle of mastication that depresses the mandible to open the mouth.

terms.sub: Temporal, Infratemporal Fossae and Muscles of Mastication
clues: A slender nerve branch that arises inside the temporal bone and crosses the medial surface of the tympanic membrane.
It exits the skull through the petrotympanic fissure to join the lingual nerve.
It carries taste fibers from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue and parasympathetic fibers to the submandibular ganglion.

terms.sub: Neck Triangles and Deep Cervical Fascia
clues: A tubular condensation of deep cervical fascia extending from the cranial base to the root of the neck.
The ansa cervicalis is embedded in or lies immediately on its anterior wall.
It encloses the common and internal carotid arteries, internal jugular vein, and vagus nerve.

terms.sub: Neck Triangles and Deep Cervical Fascia
clues: A loop of somatic motor nerves formed by superior and inferior roots from cervical ventral rami.
It lies anterior to the internal jugular vein within or on the carotid sheath.
It innervates the sternohyoid, sternothyroid, and omohyoid muscles.

terms.sub: Root of the Neck and Thyroid/Parathyroid Glands
clues: A deep lateral cervical muscle arising from the anterior tubercles of C3-C6 transverse processes and inserting on the first rib.
The subclavian vein passes anterior to it, whereas the subclavian artery and brachial plexus pass posterior to it.
The phrenic nerve descends vertically across its anterior surface beneath the prevertebral fascia.

terms.sub: Root of the Neck and Thyroid/Parathyroid Glands
clues: A branch of the vagus nerve that hooks around the right subclavian artery on the right and the aortic arch on the left.
It ascends in the tracheoesophageal groove close to the inferior thyroid artery.
It supplies all intrinsic muscles of the larynx except the cricothyroid.
A fan-shaped extrinsic muscle arising from the superior mental spine of the mandible.
It forms the bulk of the inferior part of the tongue and is innervated by the hypoglossal nerve.
Unilateral paralysis causes the protruded tongue to deviate toward the injured side.
A triangular muscle whose tendon hooks medially around the pterygoid hamulus.
It opens the auditory tube during swallowing and yawning and tenses the soft palate.
It is the only palatal muscle innervated by the mandibular nerve rather than the vagus nerve.
A paired intrinsic laryngeal muscle arising from the posterior surface of the cricoid lamina.
It inserts onto the muscular process of the arytenoid cartilage and rotates it laterally.
It is the sole abductor of the vocal folds, widening the rima glottidis during breathing.
A hyaline cartilage shaped like a signet ring positioned at the C6 vertebral level.
It articulates with the inferior horns of the thyroid cartilage and the bases of the arytenoid cartilages.
It is the only complete circumferential ring of cartilage in the entire airway.

terms.sub: Nose, Paranasal Sinuses, Orbit, and Ear
clues: A curved cleft on the lateral wall of the middle nasal meatus located just inferior to the ethmoidal bulla.
It leads anterosuperiorly into the ethmoidal infundibulum.
The frontal, anterior ethmoidal, and maxillary sinuses all drain into this groove.

terms.sub: Nose, Paranasal Sinuses, Orbit, and Ear
clues: An extraocular muscle originating from the body of the sphenoid superomedial to the optic canal.
Its round tendon passes through a fibrocartilaginous pulley on the frontal bone before inserting on the sclera.
It is the only muscle innervated by the trochlear nerve (CN IV).
